Here’s a guide to creating a digital product that actually sells (not just sits in your link in bio): 1.Start with one painful problem “Delusional mindset,” “TikTok Shop basics,” “How to ___” — your product should be a solution, not a diary. One problem, one person. 2.Pick a simple format Ebook, mini-course, or live workshop. Don’t overcomplicate the format while you’re still proving the offer. 3.Build the offer around a transformation “Go from X to Y in Z time.” People pay for what changes in their life, not how many pages or modules they get. 4.Talk about it every day I hit my first 5-figure month because I wouldn’t shut up about my offer. Stories, lives, TikToks, captions — repetition builds trust. 5.Refine instead of restarting Don’t kill a product after one “meh” week. Tweak the messaging, the promise, the bonuses. Your digital product checkout is more than a payment button. 👀 If you sell ebooks, templates, courses, guides, Canva templates, or other digital products, you need to think about what happens after someone clicks “buy.” Before selling your first digital product, make sure you have: 1️⃣ Purchase terms — what the customer is actually agreeing to when they buy. 2️⃣ License & use restrictions — what they can and cannot do with your product. 3️⃣ Privacy Policy — especially if you’re collecting customer information. 4️⃣ Website/store terms — the rules governing purchases and use of your store. 5️⃣ Protection against unauthorized sharing & reselling — because your digital product should not become the internet’s free download. 😭 Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. And remember: your legal protection shouldn’t start after someone steals or misuses your digital product. It should be part of your business from the beginning.
